findings.evidenceJa: 落雷の如くセイバーを撃つ
findings.governingReading: The active Japanese has the axe-sword come down and cut the ground past Saber; the preceding lightning-strike wording is commented out.
findings.explanation: mirror moon prints the deleted lightning version and the active comes-down version consecutively.

findings.governingReading: The mighty sword cleaves through the earth as Saber twists aside.
findings.explanation: Breaks generalizes the clean cutting action that defines the weapon’s danger.

findings.highlight: I feel like I’ll grind my teeth down
findings.governingReading: Shirou clenches so hard that his teeth feel liable to shatter.
findings.explanation: Grinding them down suggests gradual abrasion rather than imminent breakage under pressure.

findings.governingReading: Shirou concludes that cutting down the rock-like mountain requires a sword.
findings.explanation: Defeat removes the concrete cutting image that guides his choice of weapon.

findings.governingReading: The imagined king’s sword is sharp, resplendent, and knows no chipped edge.
findings.explanation: The English omits the blade’s immunity to nicking, a material quality relevant to striking Berserker.

findings.highlight: an indescribable discomfort assails me I feel like I’m going crazier
findings.evidenceJa: 言いようのない不快に包まれる
findings.governingReading: The more Shirou sees Saber near collapse, the more an indescribable revulsion or discomfort envelops him.
findings.explanation: The English prints an unpunctuated second variant about going crazier after the first rendering.

findings.governingReading: Saber coughs and briefly folds her body into a sharp angle.
findings.explanation: In pain adds an explicit cause not stated in the image.

findings.highlight: It seems like knocking down dominos The triggers
findings.evidenceJa: ドミノ倒しのようでもあり
findings.governingReading: The rising hammers resemble falling dominoes before all triggers are pulled.
findings.explanation: The English omits punctuation between the domino image and the trigger sentence.

findings.governingReading: Shirou abruptly corrects his belief that Saber was cut in half.
findings.explanation: No and that’s are fused.

findings.governingReading: Saber deliberately induces Berserker to make a wide swing.
findings.explanation: Swing and and are fused.

findings.highlight: Saber, who is right in front of him
findings.evidenceJa: 完全に懐に入ったセイバー
findings.governingReading: Saber has penetrated completely inside Berserker’s guard, leaving him no way to escape her counterattack.
findings.explanation: Right in front removes the decisive close-range positional advantage.

findings.highlight: places both hands on her sword
findings.governingReading: Saber readjusts and renews her two-handed grip.
findings.explanation: Places both hands loses the regripping action after her entry.

findings.evidenceJa: なお深く巨人に踏み込み
findings.governingReading: Saber steps still deeper into the giant before releasing her full-strength cut.
findings.explanation: The English omits the continued advance that completes her feint and close-range technique.

findings.governingReading: Rin’s primary or real attack follows Saber’s setup without delay.
findings.explanation: Final adds an unsupported claim that this is the last attack.

findings.governingReading: The active Japanese uses one German incantation line; the longer alternate wording is commented out.
findings.explanation: mirror moon activates the deleted wording and then repeats the active incantation, producing two consecutive spell variants.

findings.evidenceJa: 血でないものまで混ざっている
findings.governingReading: Shirou observes only that something clearly other than blood is mixed into the spray.
findings.explanation: The English specifically identifies spinal fluid without source support.

findings.highlight: There are things other than blood mixed in it, but I’m sure it wasn’t overkill. I can’t be too happy about it when there are things other than blood mixed in it. …But I’m sure it wasn’t overkill.
findings.evidenceJa: やりすぎという事はないだろう
findings.governingReading: Shirou notes the non-blood matter once and concludes the attack was not excessive against this monster.
findings.explanation: The English prints two competing versions, repeats both the mixed matter and overkill conclusion, and inserts a separate claim that he cannot be happy.

findings.highlight: Is Berserker’s face, though it was certainly blown away
findings.evidenceJa: バーサーカーの貌があった
findings.governingReading: As the smoke clears, Berserker’s face is there despite the certainty that his head had been blown away.
findings.explanation: The English inversion lacks a grammatical subject construction and says the face itself was blown away.

findings.highlight: his Noble Phantasm isn’t something like that
findings.governingReading: Rin realizes Berserker’s Noble Phantasm is not an external object or weapon.
findings.explanation: Something like that leaves the object-versus-body inference vague at the point of discovery.

findings.governingReading: The Noble Phantasm is written as “Twelve Labors,” with God Hand supplied as its ruby reading.
findings.explanation: The English preserves only the ruby name and removes the surface phrase that connects the ability to Heracles’ twelve trials.

findings.evidenceJa: 神々にかけられた不死の呪い
findings.governingReading: The immortality is a curse placed upon Heracles by the gods.
findings.explanation: The English omits the gods as agents and reduces the phrase to an uncaused condition.

findings.highlight: tries to tear off Berserker’s fingers
findings.governingReading: Rin tries to pry Berserker’s fingers away from her body.
findings.explanation: Tear off suggests amputating his fingers rather than breaking his grip.

findings.highlight: What lies ahead is that inescapable figure of her, miserably crushed
findings.governingReading: Shirou sees the inescapable prospective image of Rin being crushed if the tightening grip continues.
findings.explanation: The English describes a figure already crushed, prematurely converting imminent horror into completed bodily destruction.

findings.highlight: I forget who I’m against or where I am
findings.governingReading: Shirou violently casts aside all concern for what the opponent is or where he stands.
findings.explanation: Forget changes deliberate abandonment of thought into a lapse of memory.

findings.governingReading: Saber’s invisible sword descends on the defenseless arm as casually as cutting a daikon.
findings.explanation: A vegetable removes the specific domestic image and its blunt comic contrast with Berserker’s body.

findings.governingReading: Saber’s face freezes when she sees Shirou rush Berserker.
findings.explanation: Wha and Shirou are fused.

findings.evidenceJa: こっちの手がおかしくなる
findings.governingReading: The hand with which Shirou struck Berserker is itself damaged and numb.
findings.explanation: Hands pluralizes the affected limb and loses the direct blow-to-striking-hand relation.

findings.governingReading: Saber’s warning makes Shirou look up.
findings.explanation: Raise my face is Japanese-shaped physical wording for the change in gaze.

findings.governingReading: Shirou’s broken breathing accompanies his attempt to rise.
findings.explanation: Ha and Haa are fused into an uncontrolled typography error.

findings.governingReading: Saber urgently orders her Master to stop and get away.
findings.explanation: Way and that are fused, and the punctuation separating her shock from the command is absent.

findings.highlight: My body, that should have dodged the blow
findings.governingReading: Shirou’s body collapses although he believed he had dodged.
findings.explanation: Should have turns mistaken perception into a normative or counterfactual claim.

findings.evidenceJa: 出来ない事はないはずだ
findings.governingReading: Shirou insists that recreating the weapon from scratch should not be impossible if a model exists.
findings.explanation: Nothing should be impossible universalizes a claim scoped to this desperate act of reproduction.

findings.evidenceJa: 基本と構成と制作と経験と年月
findings.governingReading: His thought races through fundamentals, structure, manufacture, experience, and accumulated years.
findings.explanation: Work weakens production or making, while time removes the years of accumulation that make imitation inadequate.

findings.governingReading: Shirou glares at the giant while, behind that giant, Saber prepares the holy sword.
findings.explanation: Behind me relocates Saber to Shirou’s rear and breaks the battlefield geometry of Berserker turning toward him.

findings.highlight: Saber is determined to use her holy sword
findings.evidenceJa: 決意した姿が、網膜に焼き付いた
findings.governingReading: The sight of Saber resolving to use the holy sword despite her own disappearance burns itself onto Shirou’s retina.
findings.explanation: The English removes Shirou’s perception and the searing visual image, presenting only a flat statement of Saber’s intent.
